Script executed: ```bash sed -n 1,160p src/main/gitlab/pipeline-job-graph.ts ``` Repository: stablyai/orca Length of output: 4945 --- Script executed: ```bash rg -n 'fetchPipelineJobs|fetchPipelineBridges|fetchPipelineJobPage' src --glob '!*.test.ts' ``` Repository: stablyai/orca Length of output: 905 --- Script executed: ```bash sed -n 180,235p src/main/gitlab/pipeline-job-graph.ts echo '--- work-item-details ---' sed -n 135,175p src/main/gitlab/work-item-details.ts echo '--- base pipeline-job-graph (pre-change) ---' git show f3088d53c9cd19f0f6ad2233351fa12bbf455796:src/main/gitlab/pipeline-job-graph.ts 2>&1 | sed -n 1,140p ``` Repository: stablyai/orca Length of output: 7780 ---
**Keep already-fetched pages when a follow-up page request fails.** A failure on page 2 or later rejects `fetchAllPipelinePages` and discards every item from earlier pages. For a pipeline with more than 100 jobs, `fetchPipelineJobs` rejects and the work-item details caller turns that into an empty job list. A failed bridge page has the same effect: all bridges are dropped and child pipelines are not expanded. Before this change, the first page was returned on its own, so these outcomes are regressions. Keep the pages fetched so far when a follow-up page fails. Keep the rejection when page 1 fails.
Suggested fix
```diff --- "a/src/main/gitlab/pipeline-job-graph.ts" +++ "b/src/main/gitlab/pipeline-job-graph.ts" @@ -83,11 +83,20 @@ page === 1 ? `per_page=${PIPELINE_JOB_PAGE_SIZE}` : `per_page=${PIPELINE_JOB_PAGE_SIZE}&page=${page}` - const { stdout } = await glabExecFileAsync( - ['api', ...glabHostnameArgs(projectRef, connectionId), `${endpoint}?${query}`], - glabRepoExecOptions(repoPath, connectionId, localGitOptions) - ) - const data = JSON.parse(stdout) as T[] + let data: T[] + try { + const { stdout } = await glabExecFileAsync( + ['api', ...glabHostnameArgs(projectRef, connectionId), `${endpoint}?${query}`], + glabRepoExecOptions(repoPath, connectionId, localGitOptions) + ) + data = JSON.parse(stdout) as T[] + } catch (error) { + if (page === 1) { + throw error + } + // Keep the items from earlier pages when a follow-up page fails. + break + } if (!Array.isArray(data)) { break } ```
Add tests for two cases. First, page 1 returns 100 jobs and page 2 rejects. The call must return the 100 jobs. Second, page 1 rejects. The call must still reject.
